evidence.statement: Reachability is a real constraint on this ICP, not an accident of one bad list. Of 12 UK MSP contact pages checked on 2026-08-20, 5 published a usable commercial address, 3 obfuscated it behind Cloudflare, 2 published only a support address, and 2 published none at all. Three of the four EXP-ACQ-0001 bounces were the company's own published route rejecting or hiding external email.

A published, non-obfuscated, non-support address is NOT sufficient for reachability. AMVIA's hello@amvia.co.uk was verified on their own contact page on 2026-08-20 and hard-bounced 'address not found' six seconds after sending. 1 of 5 replacements failed on a criterion designed to prevent exactly that. Publication proves intent, not that the mailbox exists; only a send proves delivery.

EXP-CREATIVE-0001 could not be preregistered on 2026-08-21: no baseline exists for contact_intent, so success and review thresholds could only have been invented. Power analysis shows 870 sessions across both arms in the most generous case (5% baseline doubling) and 15,500 in the least (1% to 1.5%). Outbound is the only channel with real exposure and is occupied by EXP-ACQ-0001; every other channel is not_started. The constraint is audience, not experiment machinery.
evidence.source: power analysis + channels registry + empty experiment_trust_results, 2026-08-21

evidence.statement: First owned-site reading, ~24h from 2026-08-20: 47 sessions, 3 contact_intent events, 6.4% (95% CI 2.2-17.2%). CONTAMINATED: at least one event is our own verification click when confirming the instrumentation, and our sessions are in the denominator. Treat as an order-of-magnitude signal that traffic exists, not as a baseline rate. Confidence 0.6 for that reason.

EXP-ACQ-0001 reached its 50-send minimum and recorded REVIEW on 2026-08-27: 50 counted sends (55 rows, 5 bounces excluded), 0 meaningful replies, observed 0.0 against a 0.10 KEEP and 0.05 REVIEW threshold. Wilson 95% CI 0-7.1%. P(0 replies given a true 10% rate) = 0.52%, given a true 5% rate = 7.7%. The 10% hypothesis is dead for the route as executed; 5% is improbable but not excluded.
evidence.source: age import-outreach + age scoreboard + age experiment-result against experiments/EXP-ACQ-0001/sales/outreach.csv, 2026-08-27

evidence.statement: 48 of EXP-ACQ-0001's 50 counted sends went to a role inbox (info@, contact@, enquiries@, sales@, support@, cyber@, cra@, uksales@, tellmemore@); 2 reached a named buyer's own address (Blue Frontier, Technical Drive). The channel tested was cold email to a shared inbox, not cold email to a buyer. At n=2 the named-buyer route returns zero replies 81% of the time even at a true 10% rate, so it is untested and must not be reported as failed. Successor experiments must record recipient_class per send and report the two rates separately.

Internal-traffic exclusion is live in production. theplus-tech-website@79513d2 'Stop measuring ourselves' (2026-08-22 06:42 BST) drops pageviews and custom events together for a flagged session; the marker tpt_internal_traffic and the event name contact_intent are both present in the JavaScript bundle served from https://theplus-tech.com on 2026-08-27, verified by fetching every chunk from the origin rather than by reading the branch. Vercel has no retroactive filter, so the clean baseline window is 2026-08-22 to 2026-09-18 and the 20th-to-22nd traffic remains a mixture.
evidence.source: curl of https://theplus-tech.com plus grep of the served chunks, 2026-08-27

evidence.statement: EXP-ACQ-0002 preregistered 2026-08-27 to test the route EXP-ACQ-0001 never tested: the same message delivered to a named buyer's own mailbox. KEEP >=10%, ITERATE 5-9.9%, REVIEW <5% (unchanged, so the two routes stay comparable), minimum sample 30 delivered named_buyer sends. n=30 rejects KEEP if it returns zero (P=4.2% at a true 10%) but cannot reject ITERATE (P=21.5% at a true 5%); roughly 60 would be needed for that. Contact discovery is an admission gate, not a step. Zero sends executed: outreach is external surface and is proposed, not run unattended.

Contact discovery for EXP-ACQ-0002 found 0 reachable named-buyer mailboxes across 18 observed UK MSP accounts (Wilson 95% CI 0-17.6%, implying a ceiling of ~10 across all 55). Reaching the 30-send minimum would require a 54.5% publication rate; P(observing 0 in 18 at that rate) = 7e-7. EXP-ACQ-0001 independently found 2 personal addresses across 27 named accounts (7.4%, upper bound 23.4% = 13 accounts). Named decision-makers were found for essentially every account with public LinkedIn profiles: the constraint is the mailbox, not the person. Mid-market UK MSPs do not publish commercial decision-makers' addresses, so for this ICP cold email is structurally a shared-inbox channel - already measured at 0/48. EXP-ACQ-0002 does not start; its contract was not relaxed to fit the supply.

Every apparent named-buyer address in the discovery run came from an enrichment aggregator and none survived first-party verification. pjob@intergence.com was reported by a search summariser as listed in Intergence's official contact details; the contact page carries only contact@, support@ and itsupport@, and the leadership page names six people and publishes no address. Others were masked (m*****@zenzero.co.uk, l******@ramsac.com), inferred from a stated format, or mutually inconsistent (three different addresses for Wavex's CEO). An inferred address is a hypothesis about a mail server, which is where four of EXP-ACQ-0001's five lost sends died.
evidence.source: WebFetch of intergence.com/contact and /why-intergence versus search summaries, 2026-08-27

evidence.statement: LinkedIn Help states verbatim: 'Basic and free LinkedIn members can include a personalized message to five connection requests per month. LinkedIn Premium members can send unlimited personalized messages with their connection requests.' Five per month makes a 30-send minimum take six months on a free account, so the LinkedIn route cannot be run unpaid. LinkedIn does not publish its invitation thresholds ('LinkedIn Support cannot disclose the type or reason for the restriction'); the widely-quoted weekly caps and note character limits come from automation vendors selling tools to exceed them and are recorded as unverified.

LinkedIn's own compare-plans page lists Sales Navigator Core at US$119.99/month (US$1,079.88/year) and Advanced at US$159.99/month (US$1,799.88/year), both with 50 InMail credits per month. GBP figures appear on the page but were not captured; a widely-quoted GBP94.99 for Core is unverified. Sales Navigator is likely the wrong purchase: the binding constraint is personalised connection notes, which any Premium account unlocks, and Premium is cheaper. Sales Navigator's search filters and InMail credits are not needed when the account list already exists in sales/teardowns/.

The LinkedIn route is not metrically comparable to EXP-ACQ-0001. Email had one step (arrived or bounced); LinkedIn has invite -> accept -> message -> reply. A connection request is not a delivery: an unaccepted invite is never read and is not a bounce either, it is a silent non-event. Reusing the 10%/5% thresholds would compare two different quantities. The honest primary metric is a funnel with invite-accept rate as the new unknown, which has no baseline. The note is also character-limited, so the OBSERVATION + ECONOMIC HYPOTHESIS + CTA message cannot be sent as written - the channel change forces a message change, and that confound must be designed around before running, not explained afterwards.
